title: service-messaging: `EmailSenderSurface` render/send inputs declare no `currency`, so both channels pass it by a spread that escapes the excess-property check
body:
domain:server#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUCizoYWQVJWjhdR6F

Found by the delta contract review of PR #27730 (#27257), record `6509670944` (should-fix S3). The shape predates that PR (#26939); not a defect at runtime.

## What is wrong

`EmailSenderSurface.sendTemplate` / `renderTemplate` (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/email-channel.ts`) declare input types with no `currency`. The email and inbox channels pass one anyway, through a spread (`...(currency ? { currency } : {})` from #26939, and the trial-render default PR #27730 adds). The spread escapes TypeScript's excess-property check, so the type does not say what the channels send, and a rename on either side would not be caught.

## Expected

Declare `currency?: string` on both input types and pass it plainly. This widens a package-internal surface type (it is not re-exported from the package entry; check that and state it), with no behaviour change. Pin by typecheck.

Re-check after #27730 merges.

Filed without `domain:*`; grading is triage's.
